messages:
Emma: Thanks for the all-hands today — dropping quick follow-ups for leadership Q&A. Will answer over the day.
Sam: Happy to take these.
Jon: Curious re: mission language. We say "make inference accessible" — does that mean preferring developer ergonomics over raw performance wins?
Sam: We mean both. Accessibility = predictable economics + easy onboarding. We won't trade away SLOs. Example: default batching helps cost but shouldn't spike p95.
Priya: For sales decks, should we call out specific workloads where Redwood beats hyperscalers?
Sam: Yes — generative search and customer-facing chat with strict latency/p95, and regulated enterprise deployments (finance, healthcare) where private options matter.
Emma: On model catalog: will we certify community models or only curated partners?
Jon: Plan is curation + certification tiers (community, verified, verified+perf). Verified+perf has SLA/backing for production.
Priya: How do we avoid being pinned as "just another endpoint" by customers?
Maya: Emphasize operational controls (rollouts, policy routing), cost tooling (Optimize), and observability. Case studies help.
Emma: Any product tradeoffs this quarter we should know about?
Sam: Prioritizing rollout & policy UI over new hosted experimental features. Also investing in Dedicated autoscale controls.
Jon: Competitor angle — are we tracking integrated model-inference bundles? (They launch models + infra together)
Sam: Yes; they have velocity, but they often lack deployment flexibility and customer telemetry/controls. We lean into that gap.
Priya: Small request: a 1-pager that distills the mission + three buyer-facing bullets for GTM.
Sam: Will draft and share tomorrow.
R&D Bot: Note: follow-up doc created -> https://redwood.example/ah/followup-1949954321 :spiral_note_pad:
Maya: Thanks — will sync with marketing to update the pitch.
Sam: Thanks team — keep adding items here if anything else pops up.
